from.place: m-pseudo-coherence induction: pass from all m-pseudo-coherent bounds to pseudo-coherence

title: Pseudo-coherence is equivalent to m-pseudo-coherence for every m
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $D(R)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $R$-modules. For an integer $m$, call an object $C$ of $D(R)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(R)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C)$ for $i>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. Call $C$ pseudo-coherent if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules. Let $C$ be a complex of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], viewed as an object of $D(R)$. Then $C$ is pseudo-coherent if and only if $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.66.5 (Tag 064U), equivalence of pseudo-coherence and m-pseudo-coherence for every m
